subject: PMCL
disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.prereqs: Flat token list: course refs {subject, number, minGrade} joined by 'And'/'Or' strings; nested arrays are parenthesized groups. minGrade is the minimum passing grade required.
legend.coreqs: Courses that must be taken in the same term.
legend.offerings.terms: Past/scheduled terms by Banner code (YYYY = academic-year END year; Fall runs in YYYY-1). sections/enrolled/capacity are snapshots from the scheduled scrape, NOT live seat availability.
legend.offerings.typicalDays: Weekdays on which at least 50% of recent sections met.
legend.offerings.daysPct: Percent of recent sections meeting on each weekday (M/T/W/Th/F).
legend.offerings.meetingPatterns: [pattern, percent-of-sections] pairs; in patterns like 'MWR', R means Thursday.
legend.instructors: Per season. sharePct = average percent of that season's enrolled students taught by this professor (recent terms). 'reviews' links their RateMyHusky page when one exists.
legend.level: undergrad for course numbers below 5000, grad otherwise.
legend.typicallyOffered: Seasons in which the course was scheduled in at least two-thirds of that season's terms on record since it first appeared — a pattern, not a guarantee.
legend.unlocks: Courses that list this course in their prerequisites — what taking it opens up.
legend.nuPath: NUpath general-education attributes this course carries.
legend.repeatable: Whether the course may be taken more than once for credit (repeatMax / repeatMaxSH cap it).

courses.subject: PMCL
courses.title: Ion Channel Physiology and Pharmacology
courses.description: Focuses on ion channel proteins, their structure and function, as well as pharmacology. Drug action is pursued based on mechanisms used to control the gating/trafficking of ion channels that modulate their activity and cell surface localization.Introduces students to molecular modeling and dynamic simulations that can capture the gating process and ion permeation of ion channels and provide a mechanistic guide of structure-based drug design. Reviews ion channels and the drugs that target them that apply to a wide variety of medical conditions, such as arrhythmias, hypertension, epilepsy, pain, local anesthesia, cystic fibrosis, and depression. Offers students an opportunity to perform simulations on ion channels with known drugs to establish models for future lead design and development studies.

courses.subject: PMCL
courses.title: Small-Molecule Target and Ligand Pharmacology
courses.description: Focuses on ligand-gated ion channel proteins, G-protein coupled receptors and enzymes, their structure and function, as well as pharmacology. Drug action is pursued based on mechanisms used to control cell signaling and gene expression. Offers students an opportunity to apply physiologic systems and drugs used to treat related pathologies, as well as in silico modeling, to study these effects.

courses.subject: PMCL
courses.title: Pharmacology 2
courses.description: Continues PMCL 6260, although in a format that is not contingent that PMCL 6260 precedes this course.

courses.subject: PMCL
courses.title: Receptor Pharmacology
courses.description: Reviews receptors for drug substances and for endogenous ligands in a format that combines lecture presentations and discussion. Focuses on the evaluation of current literature. Covers techniques available to study receptors, various models for receptor-ligand interactions, stereochemical aspects of receptor interactions, receptor-mediated coupling mechanisms, and evaluation of several specific receptor systems.
